utterances.text: 12th of December, four lines down: "Shelling widely dispersed throughout city." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Six lines down in the same entry, I read: "The attacks upon Lukavica reported yesterday seem to have abated without causing the usual severe response against the Presidency and inner city." Do those words appear?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say, "the usual severe response," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a usual modus operandi that random shelling of the city of Sarajevo would occur if certain other events were having been brought to the attention of the Presidency side, not fulfilled.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, following Otes, that is the fighting in Otes, was there a fresh outbreak of fighting in the area of Zuc?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The 13th of December, four lines down: "Shelling throughout the city with a concentration on Zuc." Do those words appear?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please now go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please use your microphone, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Page 85 line 22, for the benefit of the booth, there is no date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the English transcript indicates that is to be corrected later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we all have seen that it was the 13th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That completes examination-in-chief, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If that document could be returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is it you who is going to cross-examine the witness? Before giving you an opportunity to do so --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just Mr. Ierace and Ms. Pilipovic, what do we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. expect the following days to happen? The examination-in-chief of Mr. Mole altogether took far more than four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but a lot of that was reading passages, objections, countless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. But At least it will take a couple of hours to cross-examine the witness. How is the schedule --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like you to -- I mean, it is you who is going to prepare for calling the next witnesses. So what do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I had in mind, Mr. President, that the cross-examination of Mr. Mole would be completed tomorrow, and following that, rather than immediately call Mr. Fraser, perhaps we could deal with some of the outstanding issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I anticipate that Mr. Fraser will be very short in chief, perhaps one hour at the very most, and that we would also on Thursday commence, if not finish, Mr. Bergeron, so that we can at least start Mr. Philips on Friday. That is a very tight schedule but it would allow for some legal argument tomorrow after Mole -- I am sorry, after Mr. Mole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say we -- tomorrow it would just be Mr. Mole then and on Thursday it would be -- perhaps I lost a bit track. But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Fraser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you earlier indicated that Mr. Fraser would be on the 15th of July, or am I mistaken?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Initially, Mr. Fraser was down for the 28th of June, and when Witness AD ran over, we indicated we would call him after Mr. Mole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Mole was still at the 15th of July and so that is where the mistake comes from. So then Mr. Fraser, and for Thursday you would say?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Fraser Thursday morning, perhaps starting tomorrow afternoon, depending on how we go with Mr. Mole and the legal issues. Following Mr. Fraser, then Mr. Bergeron, who also will be brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And then Mr. Philips on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And Mr. Philips would finish on Friday part heard, so that General Van Baal could commence Monday morning. And Mr. Philips would be back in the witness box after Mr. Van -- excuse me. Perhaps that is as far as I need it take it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that is clear to me. I am not talking in terms of optimism or pessimism because it is also a matter of the parties and how they deal with the matters. I have one question to the Defence: If there would be any additional observation to be made on 92 bis, how much time would that take? Or would you rather do it in writing, which is perfectly -- I mean, so in addition to the earlier filing, let's just assume for the sake of argument that could be considered to be a filing in response to the later filing of the Prosecution. How much time would the additional argument on 92 bis take?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind that within the framework of the Prosecutor's motion which streamlines or, rather, categorizes the statements, in particular, statements for the purposes of establishing authenticity, we still have not received the response as far as the illegibility is concerned. We are talking about a group of witnesses who would testify pursuant to 92 bis, and I think that we would need altogether 30 minutes to argue our case and also as a response to the motion of the Prosecution to introduce into evidence the statement of the late Hamdija Cavcic, also pursuant to 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say that for 92 bis you would need an 30 additional minutes, apart from what has been filed already.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it may take less than 30 minutes. I am now looking at the documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Mole.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before I proceed with the cross-examination of Mr. Mole, let me just say that we have the approval of the Chamber, for the purposes of efficiency, to -- for me to share the cross-examination with my colleague, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I will begin the cross-examination, and at one point in time, Mr. Piletta-Zanin will take over.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mole, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, can you confirm for us that on the 1st, the 2nd, the 3rd of September, 1997, you gave a statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that on the 9th and the 11th of April, 2002, you had another interview with the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mole. You took over as the commander of a group of UN military observers in the sector of Sarajevo in September 1992. Could you give us the exact date when your function started and also tell us the date when you completed it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started the 16th of September, 1992 and completed, I believe it was the 27th, 28th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, by taking over as a commander of an UNMO group, you said that the military observers were divided into two groups. One of them was working in the town of Sarajevo under the control -- that is in the part of the town which was under the BH Presidency control and that the other group was working under the territory which was under the control of the VSR. I am referring to the Papa and Lima positions.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Mole, what agreement provided for the deployment of the UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Airport Agreement, which was signed in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As part of that Airport Agreement which was signed in June 1992, was there an additional agreement which was signed as a part thereof and which referred to the collection of heavy weapon?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe it was an additional agreement. I think it was part of the Airport Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that both sides, and when I say "both sides," I am referring to the BH Presidency forces and the forces of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, that is the army of Republika Srpska, that both sides agreed to the part which referred to the collection of heavy weapon?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You testified about the positions of UN military observers, Papa and Lima positions. In view of the fact that you took over on the 16th of September, 1992, can you tell us how these two locations were selected, according to which criteria, when it comes to the deployment of UN military observers on both sides?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lists of heavy weapons were submitted to the United Nations, as was their location. So that would be one series of locations which UN observers would occupy. We were also asked to cover the city in terms of observing as much of it as possible. Those would be the two key aims of deployment of the military observers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, can you confirm for us whether this agreement which you said was submitted to the United Nations was, indeed, accepted by the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, can you identify which agreement you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the agreement which was part of the Airport Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Agreement of June 1992, which included an annex on the collection of heavy weapons. That is the agreement which served as the basis for deployment and selection of positions of UNMOs on both sides, that is the agreement which was part of the Airport Agreement and which concerned the collection of heavy weapons. You said that it had been submitted at one point to the United Nations. What I want to know is whether you have any personal knowledge whether this agreement was indeed accepted by the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You understand you speak of an agreement before I was in Sarajevo? But I understand your question. For the fact that we invoked heavy weapon collection points indicates that the United Nations accepted the Airport Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge or is it something that you have just formed your opinion on?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, do I have personal knowledge of what?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Let me try to rephrase the question. First of all, can you confirm for us that before you took over your duty, your predecessor was Mr. Richard Gray?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that Mr. Gray took part in the drafting and the signing of this agreement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, but I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, when I asked you about your personal knowledge as regards the acceptance of the agreement on the collection of heavy weapons by the United Nations, and when I wanted to know whether this was your personal opinion or personal knowledge, I was referring to the fact that Mr. Gray, who took part in the drafting and signing of this agreement, and you have just confirmed that, stated that the United Nations never actually accepted this agreement, never actually agreed to this agreement. Did you have any such information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, as regards the Airport Agreement from June 1992, in your opinion, was that agreement entered into for the purpose of disengaging the warring factions inside the town?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question reads in English: "For the purpose of disengaging the warring factions inside," and I emphasise that word, "the town." Since the witness is relying as well on the English translation, perhaps my friend could clarify what she means by "inside the town," given that the confrontation lines and the warring parties were widely dispersed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, these words --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- were words you used, I take it? I think it is the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said in the town and I was referring to the statement which I have in front of me. I can quote one line from that statement, that being the statement by the witness, Mr. Mole. For purposes of precision, I will quote and I will ask the witness to confirm for us whether that was really the case. The Airport Agreement from June 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just first, Ms. Pilipovic, finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is page 00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There are two statements, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this portion is on page 00908149 in the B/C/S version of the text in paragraph 4, and I need only one line from that statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: "The Airport Agreement from June 1992 was a small step which was taken with the purpose of separating..." "A small step taken in the attempt to separate the factions in the city." Mr. Mole, can you confirm that this is what you stated?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. You have just read two completely different sentences to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, the question is: Whether the agreement -- whether the purpose of the agreement was to separate the warring factions and I take it, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If the question is expressed in that fashion, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic. Just in order to clarify, city, town, Sarajevo, creates all kind of problems. If we are aware of that, perhaps then we would not concentrate on city itself, there are specific reasons to. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, you also stated that this was a significant agreement for the Serb side. Can you clarify, please, what you meant when you said that the agreement was a significant one for the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that the main features of the Airport Agreement involved the collection of heavy weapons which the Serb side had the majority of, and also giving up to the United Nations the airport itself which, up until the agreement, the Serb side controlled, is a significant element of the June agreement related strongly to the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if I look at the clock, would --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would have to adjourn. Mr. Mole, we are not sitting in the afternoon, we are just sitting in the morning, which means in a minute I will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00. I did not remind you this morning, but I take it was self-explanatory for you that the testimony you gave today was still under the binding of the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. The same will be true for tomorrow. I take it that you had that in mind when you testified today in this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understood that, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
